speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, can you describe exactly what sensations you are experiencing and if you have any hearing loss or tinnitus?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The symptoms of brief, spontaneous vertigo lasting only 3 minutes with a full return to baseline strongly suggest BPPV. I will not perform further questioning but will request a Dix-Hallpike test video and otoacoustic emissions to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Manifestation
